title: Income Criterion for Citizens Seeking Pro Bono Services from Legal Aid Bureau
what_it_is: Income Criterion for Citizens Seeking Pro Bono Services from Legal Aid Bureau

sections.label: Means test criteria changes
sections.summary: MinLaw intends to replace disposable income and disposable capital with Per Capita Household Income and Annual Value of residence, savings and investments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: To pass the current means test, an applicant’s disposable income cannot be more than S$10,000 per year and his disposal capital cannot be more than S$10,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Law (MinLaw) intends to adopt the Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) and the Annual Value of the applicant’s residence, savings and investments as the new criteria to replace disposable income and disposable capital.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The changes will simplify the means test, align the criteria with those under other social support schemes and shorten the application process time.

sections.label: Discretion and legal clinics
sections.summary: The Bill includes discretion, with detailed means criteria to be announced by year end, and applicants failing the means test may seek help from legal clinics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: So, there is an element of discretion that is built into the amendment Bill, as the Member might recall from the debate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: We target to announce the detailed means criteria and effect the changes by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Applicants who fail the means test may seek help from the Law Society Pro Bono Services, the Community Justice Centre and more than 50 other legal clinics run by various community, religious and voluntary welfare organisations.

sections.label: Estimated qualifying households
sections.summary: With the new amendments and criteria, approximately 25% of all households in Singapore are estimated to qualify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And we believe also that, with the discretion portion, that there will be a more judicious use of that discretion to apply to needy cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We expect, in our estimate, that with the new amendments, looking at the PCHI and the other criteria, that approximately 25% of all households in Singapore would qualify under those criteria.

sections.label: Beta version launch
sections.summary: The beta version will be launched at the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The beta version of that will be launched at the end of this year.

sections.label: Valuing legal services
sections.summary: The criteria cover valuing legal services, deciding the right lawyer or legal assistance needed, and sometimes the fees necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, the criteria are set out there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We look at it in terms of valuing legal services, deciding what is the right kind of lawyer or legal assistance that is needed and this, may on occasion, also extend to the fees that are necessary.
